edits.change: The huldu is a sleek, elongated alien swimmer about a forearm long: a smooth wedge-shaped head that flows into the neck without a break, tiny eyes set flush in the skin, no external ears, no whiskers, short paddle-like limbs held close to the body, and a long tail that tapers to a thin, flattened blade. Its proportions match no Earth mustelid, rodent or seal.

The whole body surface is smooth, fine velvet skin with a soft matte sheen and a faint dusky bloom, like the skin of a newt or a wet suede glove. No fur strands, no hair tufts, no whisker spots. The skin takes soft shading over the muscle forms beneath.

A low dorsal comb of thin, close-set rays lies folded flat along the full length of the back from the nape to the tail root, like wet fur pressed to the spine. It is a slightly darker, glossier, ridged band, clearly distinct from the velvet skin on either side. On the east profile it is the visible line along the top of the back.

One body plan on every facing: the same short paddle limbs, the same long tapering blade-tipped tail, the same velvet skin and the same flat dorsal comb. The front view, side view and rear view show this one animal turned to the camera, with the same colours and the same proportions.

The face is realistic and painterly: small dark eyes set into the head with a matte surface, a closed neutral mouth line, and a long, flat-browed wedge of a skull. The expression is calm and watchful, rendered like the animals in vanilla RimWorld.

The north view is the rear seen from behind at the game's angled camera: haunches and the root of the tail toward the viewer, the back rising and receding upward toward the head, shoulders and the back of the head visible above the haunches, eyes hidden, and the flat comb running up the centre of the spine.
Soft painted edges. Value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette: a lighter belly and a darker back separate the body from the ground. No outlines.

All three views stand at the same height, the same body width and the same head-top height, on the same foot baseline.
